docs.text:
• install-module.sh - Install a module
  • update-module.sh - Update a module
  • Module Structure - Detailed module lifecycle documentation

  3. Reads all ~/config/*.json files that define a vmid
  4. Displays a table of all running VMs with their config status
  5. Lists configured modules whose VMs are not running

  • VMs not in any config show yellow "NOT IN CONFIG"

docs.title: install-module.sh
docs.text: Deploys a TAPPaaS module with comprehensive dependency validation and service integration.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: install-module.sh <module-name> [--variant <name>] [--<field> <value>]...

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Description Example module-name Module to deploy openwebui --variant <name> Install a variant version --variant staging --<field> <value> Override JSON field --node tappaas2

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Configuration Setup — Uses copy-update-json.sh to prepare the module JSON config, supporting variant mode with automatic field derivation
  2. Dependency Validation — Confirms all services listed in dependsOn are provided by already-installed modules
  3. Service Script Verification — Ensures the module contains service scripts for each service it provides
  4. Dependency Installation — Iterates through dependsOn and calls each provider's install-service.sh
  5. Module Installation — Executes the module's install.sh if present

docs.title: Variant Mode
docs.text:
When --variant <name> is specified, the script leverages copy-update-json.sh to automatically derive:

  • vmname — Base name plus variant (e.g., openwebui-staging)
  • vmid — Next available ID after the source module
  • zone0 — Variant name if it matches a configured zone, otherwise unchanged
  • proxyDomain — Variant inserted after first domain segment

These can be overridden with explicit --<field> parameters.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Basic installation
install-module.sh vaultwarden

# With field override
install-module.sh litellm --node tappaas2

# Install staging variant (auto-derives vmname, vmid, proxyDomain)
install-module.sh openwebui --variant staging

# Variant with explicit overrides
install-module.sh openwebui --variant dev --zone0 dev-srv --vmid 315

docs.title: migrate-node.sh
docs.text: Evacuates all VMs from a Proxmox node (for maintenance) or returns them afterwards. Uses migrate-vm.sh for each individual migration.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
migrate-node.sh <node-name>
migrate-node.sh --return <node-name>
migrate-node.sh --list <node-name>

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Description Example node-name Proxmox node to evacuate tappaas1 --return <name> Return VMs that belong on this node --return tappaas1 --list <name> Dry run — show what would happen --list tappaas1 --offline Skip live migration attempts

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
1. Evacuate (migrate-node.sh tappaas1):

    • Finds all VMs currently running on the node
    • Migrates each to its configured HANode
    • VMs without an HANode are skipped with a warning

  2. Return (migrate-node.sh --return tappaas1):

    • Finds all modules whose configured node is tappaas1
    • For each VM currently running elsewhere, migrates it back
    • VMs already on the correct node are skipped

  3. List (migrate-node.sh --list tappaas1):

    • Shows both evacuate and return views without migrating
    • Color-coded: green = would migrate, yellow = no target/skipped

docs.title: Example workflow — planned maintenance
docs.text:
# 1. Check what would happen
migrate-node.sh --list tappaas1

# 2. Evacuate the node
migrate-node.sh --offline tappaas1

# 3. Perform maintenance on tappaas1
# ...

# 4. Return all VMs
migrate-node.sh --return --offline tappaas1

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Each VM migration is delegated to migrate-vm.sh, which handles HA save/restore
  • VMs without an HANode cannot be evacuated (requires manual migration)
  • The summary shows migrated/skipped/failed counts

docs.title: See Also
docs.text: • migrate-vm.sh - Migrate individual VMs between nodes

docs.title: migrate-vm.sh
docs.text: Migrates VMs between Proxmox cluster nodes. Attempts live migration first; if it fails, automatically falls back to offline migration (shutdown → migrate → start).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
migrate-vm.sh <module-name>
migrate-vm.sh --node <node-name>

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Description Example module-name Name of the module to migrate identity --node <name> Target node — migrate all its VMs back --node tappaas1 --offline Skip live migration attempt

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
1. Single module (migrate-vm.sh identity):

    • If the VM is on its primary node (node), migrates to the HA node (HANode)
    • If the VM is on its HA node, migrates back to the primary node
    • If the VM is on any other node, migrates to the primary node

  2. Node mode (migrate-vm.sh --node tappaas1):

    • Finds all modules whose configured node is tappaas1
    • For each VM not currently on that node, migrates it there
    • Useful for returning VMs after maintenance or failover

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Migrate identity to its HA node
migrate-vm.sh identity

# Force offline migration (no live attempt)
migrate-vm.sh --offline identity

# Return all VMs to tappaas1 after maintenance
migrate-vm.sh --node tappaas1

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Reads module config to determine VMID, primary node, and HA node
  2. Queries the cluster to find where the VM is currently running
  3. Saves HA state (resource + affinity rule) before migration
  4. Attempts live migration (unless --offline)
  5. Falls back to offline migration if live fails
  6. Restores HA resource and affinity rule after migration
  7. Replication direction is automatically updated by Proxmox

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Live migration may fail on clusters with different CPU architectures (e.g., Intel + AMD). The script handles this gracefully by falling back to offline migration
  • HA affinity rules are saved and restored automatically
  • The --node mode shows a summary of migrated/skipped/failed VMs

docs.text: • migrate-node.sh - Evacuate or return all VMs on a node

docs.title: repository.sh
docs.text: Manages module repositories for the TAPPaaS platform. Supports adding, removing, modifying, and listing external module repositories alongside the main TAPPaaS repository.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: repository.sh <command> [options]

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command Description add <url> [--branch <branch>] Add a new module repository remove <name> [--force] Remove a module repository modify <name> [--url <url>] [--branch <branch>] Modify a repository list List all tracked repositories

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Add a community module repository
repository.sh add github.com/someone/tappaas-community

# Add with a specific branch
repository.sh add github.com/someone/tappaas-community --branch develop

# List all repositories
repository.sh list

# Switch a repository to a different branch
repository.sh modify tappaas-community --branch stable

# Change a repository's URL
repository.sh modify tappaas-community --url github.com/other/repo --branch stable

# Remove a repository
repository.sh remove tappaas-community

# Force remove even if modules are installed from it
repository.sh remove tappaas-community --force

docs.title: What add does
docs.text:
1. Validates the repository URL is reachable via git ls-remote
  2. Clones the repository to /home/tappaas/<name>/
  3. Checks out the specified branch (default: stable)
  4. Verifies the repo contains src/modules.json
  5. Warns on VMID or module name conflicts with existing repos
  6. Updates configuration.json with the new repository entry

docs.title: What remove does
docs.text:
1. Checks that no installed modules have their location pointing into the repository
  2. Removes the repository directory
  3. Updates configuration.json to remove the repository entry

docs.title: What modify does
docs.text:
• Branch-only change: Fetches and checks out the new branch in place
  • URL change: Validates new repo has all currently-installed modules, re-clones, and updates module location fields

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Repository URLs use the same format as upstreamGit (without https:// prefix)
  • The main TAPPaaS repository is the first entry in the repositories array
  • All repositories are treated equally — no special handling for the main repo
  • VMID and module name conflicts are warnings, not errors

docs.title: See Also
docs.text: • Git Structure - Repository organization and GitOps workflow

docs.title: resize-disk.sh
docs.text: Resizes the disk of a VM both in Proxmox and inside the VM filesystem.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: resize-disk.sh <vmname> <new-size>

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Description Example vmname Name of the VM (must have a JSON config) nextcloud new-size New disk size (G, M, T, K suffix) 50G

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# Resize nextcloud disk to 50GB
resize-disk.sh nextcloud 50G

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Validates that the new size is larger than the current size (shrinking not supported)
  2. Resizes the disk in Proxmox using qm resize
  3. Connects to the VM via SSH and resizes the partition and filesystem:
  4. NixOS: Uses sfdisk to grow the partition, then resize2fs for ext4
  5. Debian/Ubuntu: Uses growpart to grow the partition, then resize2fs for ext4
  6. Verifies the new filesystem size
  7. Updates the diskSize field in the VM's JSON configuration

docs.text: OS Filesystem Status NixOS ext4 Fully supported Debian/Ubuntu ext4 Fully supported Other Any Proxmox disk resized, manual filesystem resize required

docs.text:
• SSH access to the VM as tappaas user with sudo
  • SSH access to the Proxmox node as root
  • VM must be running and reachable

docs.title: snapshot-vm.sh
docs.text: Manages VM snapshots on the Proxmox cluster for an installed module.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: snapshot-vm.sh <module-name> [--list | --cleanup <N> | --restore <N>]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Description Example module-name Name of the module (must have config in ~/config) vaultwarden --list List all snapshots on the VM --cleanup <N> Delete all snapshots except the last N --cleanup 3 --restore <N> Restore snapshot N steps back (1 = most recent) --restore 1

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Create a new snapshot
snapshot-vm.sh vaultwarden

# List all snapshots
snapshot-vm.sh vaultwarden --list

# Keep only the last 3 snapshots
snapshot-vm.sh vaultwarden --cleanup 3

# Restore to the most recent snapshot
snapshot-vm.sh vaultwarden --restore 1

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Validates the module has a config in ~/config with a vmid
  2. Verifies the VM exists on the configured Proxmox node
  3. Performs the requested snapshot operation via qm snapshot/qm rollback/qm delsnapshot

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Snapshot names follow the format tappaas-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS
  • Restore stops the VM, rolls back, then starts it again
  • Cleanup deletes oldest snapshots first

docs.title: test-module.sh
docs.text: Tests a TAPPaaS module with dependency-recursive service testing.

docs.title: Usage

docs.title: Parameters

docs.title: What it does

  2. Checks that dependency services have test-service.sh scripts

  4. Calls the module's own test.sh (if present)
  5. Reports structured results with pass/fail/skip counts

docs.text: Code Meaning 0 All tests passed 1 One or more tests failed 2 Fatal error (requires rollback/reinstall)

  • TAPPAAS_DEBUG=1 — same as --debug

docs.title: update-cron.sh
docs.text: Creates a cron entry to run the TAPPaaS update scheduler every hour.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: update-cron.sh

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Removes any existing update-tappaas cron entries
  • Creates a new cron entry for user tappaas to run hourly (at minute 0)
  • The update-tappaas command handles all scheduling logic internally, checking the global updateSchedule to determine if updates should run

docs.title: Cron entry created
docs.text: 0 * * * * /home/tappaas/bin/update-tappaas

docs.title: Why hourly?
docs.text: Running hourly ensures the scheduled hour will be matched. The update-tappaas script only performs updates when the current hour matches the global updateSchedule hour.

docs.title: update-module.sh
docs.text: Updates a TAPPaaS module safely with snapshot, testing, and automatic rollback.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: update-module.sh [options] <module-name>

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --force Proceed even if pre-update test fails --debug Show Debug-level messages --silent Suppress Info-level messages

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Creates a pre-update VM snapshot (rollback safety net)
  2. Runs test-module.sh pre-update — aborts if tests fail (unless --force)
  3. Runs the module's pre-update.sh hook (if present)
  4. Iterates dependsOn and calls each provider's update-service.sh
  5. Calls the module's own update.sh
  6. Runs test-module.sh post-update — rolls back on fatal failure

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Update succeeded, all tests passed 1 Update completed but post-update test failed (non-fatal) 2 Fatal error (rollback attempted if snapshot exists)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
update-module.sh vaultwarden
update-module.sh --force litellm
update-module.sh --debug openwebui

docs.title: update-os.sh
docs.text: Updates a VM's operating system based on its type (NixOS or Debian/Ubuntu).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: update-os.sh <vmname> <vmid> <node>

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Description Example vmname Name of the VM nextcloud vmid Proxmox VM ID 610 node Proxmox node name tappaas1

docs.title: Example
docs.text: update-os.sh myvm 610 tappaas1

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Waits for VM to get an IP address (via guest agent or DHCP leases)
  2. Updates SSH known_hosts
  3. Detects OS type (NixOS or Debian/Ubuntu)
  4. For NixOS:
  5. Runs nixos-rebuild using ./<vmname>.nix in current directory
  6. Reboots VM to apply configuration
  7. Waits for VM to come back up
  8. For Debian/Ubuntu:
  9. Waits for cloud-init to complete
  10. Runs apt-get update && apt-get upgrade
  11. Installs QEMU guest agent
  12. Fixes DHCP hostname registration via NetworkManager

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• For NixOS VMs: ./<vmname>.nix must exist in current directory
  • SSH access to VM as tappaas user
  • QEMU guest agent installed on VM
